  • In one side of the rootstock, a sanding cut of 2.5 cm in length going to a depth of half

  • Advantages of Budding
  • Rapid reproduction: Budding allows for quick generation of new individuals, which
  • can be advantageous in stable environments or when resources are abundant.
  • Energy efficiency: Budding doesn't require energy-intensive processes like gamete
  • formation, making it a more efficient reproductive strategy.
  • Suitable for stable environments: In stable environments, the lack of genetic diversity
  • may not be a significant disadvantage as the cloned offspring are well-adapted to their
  • environment.
  • Faster fruit bearing in plants: Budding can be used to produce fruit more quickly than
  • grafting in some plant species.
  • Disadvantages of Budding
  • Lack of genetic diversity: Budding produces genetically identical offspring, limiting
  • the potential for adaptation to changing environments.
  • Vulnerability to disease: The lack of genetic diversity can make populations more
  • susceptible to diseases that affect the parent organism.
  • Limited adaptability: In variable environments, the lack of genetic variation can make
  • it difficult for the cloned offspring to survive and adapt to new conditions.
